claims.text: As-received Q235 steel contains inherent surface non-metallic inclusions and segregated secondary phases produced during manufacturing.
Non-metallic inclusions in untreated Q235 steel act as localized cathodic sites.
Segregated second-phase particles in untreated Q235 steel act as localized cathodic sites.
Cathodic surface heterogeneities form localized galvanic couples with the surrounding steel matrix.
Localized galvanic coupling initiates pitting corrosion in untreated Q235 steel.
Electrochemical polishing in dilute sulfuric acid can selectively remove surface inclusions and segregated phases from Q235 steel.
The proposed electrochemical polishing treatment does not fundamentally alter the bulk microstructure.
Removing surface inclusions and segregated phases produces a more homogeneous surface-potential distribution.
A more homogeneous surface-potential distribution decreases localized galvanic interactions.
Decreasing localized galvanic interactions suppresses the onset of localized corrosion.
Electrochemically polished Q235 specimens will have a lower overall corrosion rate than untreated specimens in 3.5 wt.% NaCl at approximately 25 °C.
Electrochemically polished Q235 specimens will have a lower overall corrosion rate than untreated specimens in 3.5 wt.% NaCl at approximately 80 °C.
Electrochemical polishing will significantly reduce pit density and pit severity relative to untreated Q235 at both tested temperatures.
The proposed mechanism applies from room temperature to approximately 80 °C in 3.5 wt.% NaCl when surface inclusions are the dominant driver of localized corrosion.
Changes in surface-oxide characteristics caused by polishing could independently affect corrosion behavior.
Residual stress may independently influence pitting and confound attribution of corrosion changes to inclusion removal.
SEM/EDS can be used to verify whether polishing removed the targeted surface inclusions.

Failure to obtain a statistically significant reduction in both localized pitting density and overall corrosion rate, or worsening after polishing, would falsify the claim that surface inclusions are the dominant corrosion driver.
